correctness.rationale: Independently expanded g_s(x)=(1+s)x−s x³ and composed g_(1/2)∘g_2. Exact SymPy factorization yields F(x)−x=x(x²−1)(2x²−1)(4x⁴−12x²+7)/2, with nine real distinct roots 0, ±1, ±1/√2, ±√((3±√2)/2). Exact derivative has multipliers 9/2 at 0, 0 at ±1 and ±1/√2, and 27±18√2 at other roots, all repelling (the smaller >1). Phase identities g2(1/√2)=√2, g1/2(√2)=1/√2 imply nonoptimal 2-cycle with losses 1/16 and 1/4, average 5/32. Each root simple as fixed-point equation (F′−1≠0); all multipliers avoid unit circle; implicit-function continuation and degree-9 leading coefficient b a³≠0 prove exactly nine real roots with same stability in a small open rate neighborhood, and both nonoptimal branches remain distinct from minima. The proof does not assert no higher-epoch-period attractors.
